plain_english_policy: This bill creates a new type of hunting and fishing license specifically for disabled veterans in Alabama who have been certified as having one-hundred percent service-connected permanent disability. The licenses are valid continuously (no annual renewal required) while the veteran maintains their residency status, replacing standard resident hunting/fishing licenses but not exempting holders from specific requirements like permits to hunt on state wildlife management areas or migratory waterfowl.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would establish a continuous-validity special license for 100% disabled veterans, simplifying compliance by removing annual renewal obligations while maintaining restrictions tied to specific hunting zones and species (e.g., migratory birds). It introduces a nominal $1 issuance fee per license.
sponsorship_supports_position: Senator Means advanced this bill to provide continuous licensing for 100% disabled veterans.
evidence_quotes: "This bill would establish a special disabled veteran's hunting and freshwater and saltwater fishing license to be valid on a continuous basis for veterans showing proof of one-hundred percent, service-connected, permanent and total disability."
"The licenses issued pursuant to this section shall be valid on a continuous basis for veterans showing proof of one-hundred percent, service-connected, permanent and total disability."
